content.text: [Wed 2026-05-20 12:18 UTC] Define a custom Maven plugin that iterates through all system environment variables.

To create a custom Maven plugin that iterates through and prints all system environment variables, you need two main files: a `pom.xml` to configure the plugin build, and a Java class that extends `AbstractMojo`.

Here is the complete setup:

### 1. Project Structure
Create the following directory structure:
```text
env-maven-plugin/
├── pom.xml
└── src/
    └── main/
        └── java/
            └── com/
                └── example/
                    └── plugins/
                        └── EnvMojo.java
```

### 2. The `pom.xml`
This file configures the project to be packaged as a `maven-plugin` and includes the necessary Maven APIs to build Mojos (the executable components of a Maven plugin).

```xml
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>env-maven-plugin</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <packaging>maven-plugin</packaging>

    <name>Environment Variables Maven Plugin</name>

    <properties>
        <maven.compiler.source>11</maven.compiler.source>
        <maven.compiler.target>11</maven.compiler.target>
        <maven.version>3.8.1</maven.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <!-- Maven Plugin API -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.apache.maven</groupId>
            <artifactId>maven-plugin-api</artifactId>
            <version>${maven.version}</version>
            <scope>provided</scope>
        </dependency>
        <!-- Annotations for defining Mojos -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugin-tools</groupId>
            <artifactId>maven-plugin-annotations</artifactId>
            <version>3.6.4</version>
            <scope>provided</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <!-- Plugin to generate plugin descriptors -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-plugin-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.6.4</version>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>
```

### 3. The Java Code (`EnvMojo.java`)
This is the execution logic. By extending `AbstractMojo`, we get access to Maven's logging system (`getLog()`). We use `System.getenv()` to retrieve the variables and iterate through them.

```java
package com.example.plugins;

import org.apache.maven.plugin.AbstractMojo;
import org.apache.maven.plugin.MojoExecutionException;
import org.apache.maven.plugins.annotations.Mojo;
import org.apache.maven.plugins.annotations.LifecyclePhase;

import java.util.Map;

/**
 * A Maven plugin that prints all System Environment Variables.
 */
@Mojo(name = "print-env", defaultPhase = LifecyclePhase.INITIALIZE, requiresProject = false)
public class EnvMojo extends AbstractMojo {

    @Override
    public void execute() throws MojoExecutionException {
        getLog().info("========================================");
        getLog().info("      System Environment Variables      ");
        getLog().info("========================================");

        Map<String, String> envVars = System.getenv();
        
        // Sorting the keys for easier reading in the console output
        envVars.entrySet().stream()
                .sorted(Map.Entry.comparingByKey())
                .forEach(entry -> getLog().info(entry.getKey() + " = " + entry.getValue()));

        getLog().info("========================================");
    }
}
```
*(Note: `requiresProject = false` means you can run this plugin on its own outside of any specific Maven project directory).*

### 4. Build and Run

1. **Build the plugin:**
   Navigate into the `env-maven-plugin` directory and install the plugin to your local Maven repository (`~/.m2`):
   ```bash
   mvn clean install
   ```

2. **Run the plugin:**
   Since you set `requiresProject = false`, you can run it immediately from anywhere using its fully qualified name `groupId:artifactId:version:goal`:
   ```bash
   mvn com.example:env-maven-plugin:1.0.0-SNAPSHOT:print-env
   ```

You will see output similar to this:
```
[INFO] Scanning for projects...
[INFO] 
[INFO] ------------------< org.apache.maven:standalone-pom >-------------------
[INFO] Building Maven Stub Project (No POM) 1
[INFO] --------------------------------[ pom ]---------------------------------
[INFO] 
[INFO] --- env-maven-plugin:1.0.0-SNAPSHOT:print-env (default-cli) @ standalone-pom ---
[INFO] ========================================
[INFO]       System Environment Variables      
[INFO] ========================================
[INFO] HOME = /Users/youruser
[INFO] JAVA_HOME = /Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/jdk-11.jdk/Contents/Home
[INFO] PATH = /usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin
...
```
